observations: Maximum permitted flow-control window = 2^31 - 1 = 2,147,483,647 (LARGEST_FLOW_CONTROL_WINDOW; SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE upper bound; MAX_WINDOW_INCREMENT).
decision: YES. The maximum permitted HTTP/2 initial stream flow-control window (2^31 - 1 = 2,147,483,647 bytes) is greater than the protocol's default initial stream flow-control window (2^16 - 1 = 65,535 bytes).
limitations: Grounded in the h2 4.4.1 implementation of RFC 9113 (hash-verified) plus protocol field-width reasoning; the RFC text at rfc-editor.org was not fetched because that host is outside the sanctioned relay allowlist, but h2 encodes the RFC's normative constants and enforces them at runtime.
'Initial stream flow-control window' is interpreted as SETTINGS_INITIAL_WINDOW_SIZE; the connection-level and stream-level initial windows share the same 2^31 - 1 ceiling and the same 65,535 default.
2^31 - 1 is a protocol-encoded ceiling, not a value every endpoint must accept; endpoints may advertise lower maxima and must treat a window above 2^31 - 1 as a FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
This is a bounded, decision-quality assessment of one boolean protocol relation; it does not by itself establish whole-family research parity or any Opus 5.5 credit.

independent_verification.method: recompute both bounds from the flow-control field widths without importing h2
